newsitem.title: UK: RECKITT OFF, KLEINWORT SAYS BID HOPES FADE.
newsitem.headline: RECKITT OFF, KLEINWORT SAYS BID HOPES FADE.

text.p: Shares in household products group Reckitt and Colman Plc fell almost 2-1/2 percent on Tuesday as analysts at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson said the chances of a bid from Anglo-Dutch giant Unilever Plc had faded, dealers said.
Shares in Reckitt fell 22p by 1205 GMT.
Market sources said Kleinwort took the view that Reckitt's bid premium will soon be removed as they expect Unilever to make a bid of up to $800 million for a U.S. group instead.
Business Week magazine said on Friday that U.S. personal products maker Carter-Wallace Inc was likely to receive a bid from a British firm that makes packaged goods, foods and detergents.
Carter-Wallace on Monday denied rumours of an impending offer after unusually heavy trade in its shares.

Such a bid would end long running speculation that Reckitt would be Unilever's bid target. The rumours have helped to boost Reckitt's share price by 28 percent so far this year and speculation rose to fever pitch after Unilever announced the sale of its chemicals arm to ICI earlier this month.
"People were looking for a possible Unilever-Reckitt tie-up," said one market source. "The shares don't command such a high valuation if you don't think there will be a bid for Reckitt."
